issue_title: Refactor reentrancy detector into three variants
issue_body:
The reentrancy detector is split into three variants to facilitate the triage of results.
- `reentrancy-eth`: theft of ether and read before writing (high severity)
- `reentrancy-no-eth`: no theft of ether and read before writing (medium severity)
- `reentrancy-benign`: no read before writing (low severity)

The read before writing heuristic allows triaging benign reentrancies, where the exploitation would act as a double call.

issue_body:
# Issue
There has been a known bug in which `ActiveState.recent_block_hashes` would not hold the requisite block hashes to validate all potential attestations when it came time during a state recalc. This was due to the list of hashes always being truncated to fit the `2 * CYCLE_LENGTH` requirement even though an attestation could be from longer than that ago when considering large slot skips.

# Proposed solution
I propose that we only append to `recent_block_hashes` until the end of a state recalc, during which we remove CYCLE_LENGTH hashes. In the normal case, the length of `recent_block_hashes` will range between `2 * CYCLE_LENGTH` and `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH`. The length of `recent_block_hashes` might exceed `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH` temporarily during block processing/state recalc, but will always be trimmed down to size at the end.

EDIT: this also allows the `get_block_hash` function/`active_state.recent_block_hashes` to be more usable for during reward calculations. The current spec required using extra DB/local support for tracking hashes.
concatenated_comments:
>  * Set `active_state.recent_block_hashes = active_state.recent_block_hashes[CYCLE_LENGTH:]` 

Are you sure you don't want  * Set `active_state.recent_block_hashes = active_state.recent_block_hashes[-CYCLE_LENGTH:]` (see the minus before CYCLE_LENGTH) ? | No, I think I want to trim off a cycle worth of hashes per cycle transition. Note, that this is the a part of the cycle transition, not the dynasty. So if we do two cycle transitions in due to slot skips, we would trim off `2 * CYCLE_LENGTH` (one cycle length at a time).

After all of this is complete, if the block was not exactly on the cycle boundary, we would have `len(recent_block_hashes) > 2 * CYCLE_LENGTH` because over the course of a cycle, we append up to cycle_length hashes.
 | Note, I just fixed a bug in `append_to_recent_block_hashes`
https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/44/commits/57cbc5434cad66113dd049f0c9ef737272826a59 | > attestation could be from longer than that ago when considering large slot skips

Here, do you mean when `block.slot >= parent_block.slot + CYCLE_LENGTH`?
1. Please correct me if I'm wrong, was `active_state.recent_block_hashes` designed for easily getting `get_block_hash`? Alternatively, any chance if we can update `active.recent_block_hashes` **after** attestation validation, so that we can use the `active.recent_block_hashes` in the context of parent block?

2. Increasing the size of `active_state.recent_block_hashes` might also increase the serialization time of calculating `active_state_root`, although just a little bit I guess. I wonder if it's necessary to be in-protocol? Or we can just allocate a memory to calculate it? | `recent_block_hashes` is designed to be able to ensure that you have the block hashes required to process the current state transition on hand. The `prev_active_state + prev_crystallized_state + current_block` should be able to compute the state transition for the new active_state and crystallized_State.  The spec as is forgets hashes to quickly from `recent_block_hashes` for this to be the case.

After a state transition in the current proposed spec, the `active_state.recent_block_hashes` is never greater than `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH`

Only sometimes in the middle of a state transition are you holding greater than `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH` recent_block_hashes in memory. The pruning of CYCLE_LENGTH block hashes per state recalc ensures this. | A normal case looks like the following.

- At the beginning of a cycle (slot N), `len(recent_block_hashes) == 2 * CYCLE_LENGTH`
- when a block comes in at `slot N+1`, we append a new hash to `recent_block_hashes`
- We continue to do this until `slot N+CYCLE_LENGTH` (so we have `len(recent_block_hashes) == 3 * CYCLE_LENGTH`) at which point we compute the state recalc and prune CYCLE_LENGTH hashes off of `recent_block_hashes` after the transition
- we are back to where we started and repeat! plus we didn't get rid of any hashes in the active state until we were certain we didn't need them anymore.

Now think of an exceptional case:
- At the beginning of a cycle (slot N), `len(recent_block_hashes) == 2 * CYCLE_LENGTH`
- when a block comes in at `slot N+1`, we append a new hash to `recent_block_hashes`
- The next block that comes in is at `slot N + CYCLE_LENGTH*2 + 1` which causes us to (temporarily during the state transition append an additional `CYCLE_LENGTH*2` hashes to `recent_block_hashes`
- We now process two cycle transitions (because we passed two cycle boundaries). After the first, we remove `CYCLE_LENGTH` hashes. After the second, we remove an additional `CYCLE_LENGTH` hashes. and we had all the parent hashes we might have needed to process attestations that came in before the big skip
- Now we are left with `len(recent_block_hashes) == 2 * CYCLE_LENGTH + 1`. Note the `+ 1` is expected because we transitioned the cycle 1 slot past the cycle boundary.

Let me know if this makes sense to you. Happy to provide more clarifying content. Had to write that really quick about to be AFK | 
> After a state transition in the current proposed spec, the `active_state.recent_block_hashes` is never greater than `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH`

> Only sometimes in the middle of a state transition are you holding greater than `3 * CYCLE_LENGTH` recent_block_hashes in memory. The pruning of CYCLE_LENGTH block hashes per state recalc ensures this.

Yep! But my point was, although it’s in memory, it still larger the source of calculating `active_state_root` per block. But I see your point that it’s probably unavoidable.

The exceptional case looks correct to me. 👍 
 | You only calculate the new `active_state_root` at the end of a state transition, and the current scheme guarantees to trim the size of `recent_block_hashes` down to `< 3 * CYCLE_LENGTH` by the end of the state transition so I don't think it's really an issue.
